records.issue_text: retryCount update inside the catch block can itself throw, aborting the whole loop and skipping remaining reminders (per-reminder failure becomes batch-wide abort)
records.rationale: In the new `catch (error)` block, the code does `await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` before logging. If that update throws (e.g., DB connectivity/constraint issue), the exception is not caught (there’s no nested try/catch), so it will escape the catch block and abort the surrounding `for` loop, skipping remaining reminders. Previously the catch only logged and would continue; this failure mode is introduced by the diff.

records.issue_text: Off-by-one boundary on retry cap: retryCount: { gt: 1 } allows 3 total attempts before deletion instead of the intended 2
records.rationale: The diff shows failed attempts increment `retryCount` by 1 (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`), and the cleanup deletes reminders with `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` (i.e., `>= 2`). Since the `deleteMany` happens before fetching/processing reminders, any reminder that has failed twice will be deleted before a third attempt. This contradicts the claim that `gt: 1` allows 3 total attempts before deletion.
records.stripped_text: Off-by-one boundary on retry cap: retryCount: { gt: 1 } allows 3 total attempts before deletion instead of the intended 2

records.issue_text: Retried reminders exceeding retryCount 1 are hard-deleted instead of being marked failed/cancelled, silently dropping reminders after failures
records.rationale: The diff explicitly hard-deletes reminders once `retryCount > 1`: `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { OR: [..., { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }] } })`. Since `retryCount` is incremented on failure paths (`data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 }`), failed reminders will be removed on subsequent runs rather than being preserved/marked failed/cancelled, which is silent dropping/data loss as described.
records.stripped_text: Retried reminders exceeding retryCount 1 are hard-deleted instead of being marked failed/cancelled, silently dropping reminders after failures

records.issue_text: New OR branch in deleteMany drops the method filter and date constraint, deleting successfully-scheduled SMS reminders (silent data loss) without cancelling the Twilio message
records.rationale: The new `deleteMany` filter adds an `OR` branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` or `scheduledDate` constraint. This can delete any `WorkflowReminder` record (including non-SMS and/or not-past-due) once `retryCount > 1`. Also, the diff increments `retryCount` on failure (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`) but does not reset it on success, so a reminder that eventually succeeds could still be deleted later solely due to `retryCount > 1` (data loss). The diff shows no Twilio cancellation tied to this deletion.

records.issue_text: Successful retries never reset retryCount to 0, leaving stale retryCount on a scheduled reminder that can later trigger deletion
records.rationale: The diff introduces deletion of any WorkflowReminder with `retryCount > 1` via `deleteMany({ where: { OR: [..., { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }] } })`. The retryCount is incremented on failures (`data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 }` in both the `else` branch and `catch`), but on success the update only sets `scheduledDate`/`referenceId` etc. and never resets `retryCount` to 0. Therefore a reminder that fails a couple times and later succeeds will retain `retryCount > 1` and can be deleted on the next run purely due to the new deletion condition.

records.issue_text: Catch block treats all exceptions as retryable, including permanent failures like Twilio auth errors, which can cascade into mass deletion of all pending reminders on the next run
records.rationale: The diff makes *all* scheduling failures increment `retryCount` (both the `else` branch and the `catch` do `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`), without distinguishing retryable vs permanent errors. On the next runs, the job begins by deleting reminders with `retryCount > 1` via `deleteMany({ where: { OR: [..., { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }] } })`. That second OR condition is unconditional (not scoped to SMS or dates), so repeated permanent failures (e.g., Twilio auth) will drive reminders over the threshold and then be deleted, including still-pending reminders.
